# Testament of Zebulun — 6
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1** The record of the words of Zebulun, which he enjoined upon his sons before he died in the hundred and fourteenth year of his life. **2** He said to them: Hearken to me, ye sons of Zebulun, attend to the words of your father. **3** I, Zebulun, was a good gift to my parents, for when I was born my father was increased in flocks and herds, and while my mother was bearing me he was increased in everything, both cattle and fields. **4** I am not conscious that I have sinned all my days, save in thought. **5** Nor do I remember that I have done any iniquity, except the sin of ignorance which I committed against Joseph; for I covenanted with my brethren not to tell my father what had been done to Joseph. **6** But I wept in secret many days because of him, for I feared my brethren, because they had all agreed that if any one should declare the secret, he should be slain. **7** But when they wished to kill him, I adjured them with many tears not to be guilty of this sin.

**2** For Simeon and Gad came against Joseph to kill him. And he said to them with tears: Pity me, my brethren, have mercy upon the bowels of Jacob our father; lay not your hands upon me to shed innocent blood, for I have not sinned against you. **2** And if I have indeed sinned, chastise me with discipline, but lay not your hand upon me, for the sake of our father Jacob. **3** And as he spoke these words, weeping the while, I was unable to bear his lamentations, and I began also to weep, and my liver was poured out, and all the substance of my bowels was loosened. **4** And Joseph also wept, and I wept with him; and the whole earth trembled at our voice. **5** And I stood up against my brethren, and said: We will not slay him, but let us cast him into one of these dry pits, which our fathers digged and found no water in; for the Lord forbid that we should destroy our brother.

**3** And Simeon and Gad laid hold of Joseph to kill him; and I fell on my face before their feet, entreating them on behalf of Joseph. **2** And they pushed me aside and said: Forbear; what dost thou weep and intercede for him? He spied on us, and came to Dothan to see our doings. **3** And Judah took him away from them, according to the word of my father Jacob; and the Midianites came while Judah was absent, and drew up Joseph out of the pit, and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of gold. **4** And our brethren were ashamed and came and told our father that a wild beast had devoured Joseph; and they brought his coat and dipped it in the blood of a kid. **5** And my father mourned for Joseph many days.

**4** And after this I had great sorrow and grief, for I mourned for Joseph continually. **2** For from that time I took upon myself to serve the poor and the sick and to be compassionate to all who had need; **3** for I had been moved to compassion for the crying of Joseph, and I purposed thenceforth to be compassionate toward all. **4** For this cause, my children, I tell you to have compassion for every man; and to do good to all: rich and poor, sick and weak, stranger and neighbour; and to offer bread to the hungry. **5** Now hear me, my children, and love the Lord God with all your strength, and love one another in truth of heart.

**5** For I perceive that the hardening of your hearts is the mother of all wickedness; for by it a man forsaketh God and sinneth against men, and because of his pride he robbeth others. **2** He that hath pity upon a man supplieth lack; but he that is rich in goods and hard of heart shall receive punishment. **3** For if a man have bowels of mercy, he hath more than all things that are given to men; but if a man give not of his goods with mercy, he hath no portion with those who are compassionate. **4** For, my sons, compassion is the gift of God, and if one have it, he shall find mercy before God; but he that hath it not shall be desolate before God. **5** Have compassion therefore upon your neighbours, and be not hard upon strangers; for God will set a hard one upon you, and he will not be appeased by any prayer or sacrifice of yours.

**6** For to what extent a man hath compassion on his neighbours, to that extent also hath the Lord upon him. **2** For when we went down into Egypt, Joseph bore no malice against us, but loved us as his own soul, and enriched us all, and gave us abundant clothing, and his children served us all the days of our lives. **3** Whom then should ye obey but God, who made heaven and earth, and who filled all things with his goodness? And in compassion walketh a man perfectly before God. **4** Therefore, my children, love the Lord your God with all your heart, and love one another: and God will give you rest from all your enemies, and will deliver you from every evil.

**7** And when Zebulun had said these things, he fell asleep in a good old age. And his sons did as he had bidden them, and they carried him away and buried him in Hebron with his fathers.

---
*End of Testament of Zebulun*
